sources.title: Mihai Manea, Non-Cooperative Games, dated 19 January 2017 (MIT 14.126 Spring 2016 course hosting)
sources.reuse: Same exact URL/ID agreed with C06 author; retained original PDF/text unchanged. C07 adds actual inspected scopes.
sources.use: Sections 9–12: extensive form, perfect recall, realization-equivalence construction, subgames/backward induction and discounted one-shot proof. Sections 16–17 and 19: assessments, consistency and agent-form perfection. Section 25: normalized repeated payoffs, security/feasibility and Nash-reversion folk construction. Section 30 opening: commitment-type reputation mechanism.
limits: Theorem 19 invokes an adaptation of the one-shot principle rather than proving the information-set step. C07 supplies its own Bayes cancellation/positive-reach limit and last-deviation proof.
The chapter explicitly prunes structural zero-probability chance paths and states finite perfect recall; fully mixed behavior then reaches every remaining information set.

Theorem 22 informs the restricted Nash-reversion result; C07 supplies exact conditional public-signal inequalities. The broader minmax theorem beginning at page 66 is context, not a claimed complete inspected/proved extension.
Pages 84–87 support the role of private commitment. The source centipede example, long-run reputation bounds and empirical narrative are not imported as results proved here.

Neighboring auction, bargaining, proper-equilibrium and imperfect-monitoring text incidentally encountered is outside relied-on scope. Missing cross-reference placeholders and source examples are not copied.

sources.title: Muhamet Yildiz, Graduate Game Theory, Spring 2022 (MIT 14.126 Spring 2024 course hosting)
sources.reuse: Same exact URL/ID agreed with C06 author; retained original PDF/text unchanged. C07 adds actual inspected scopes.
sources.mapping: Cover physical page 1; substantive printed page = physical page minus 8.
sources.use: Printed pages 19–20: remembered-history construction and Kuhn equivalence context. Printed 104–111: assessments, Bayes consistency and cautions on PBE conventions. Printed 114–115: agent-normal representation, separate trembles and the perfection/sequential implication.
limits: The source states Kuhn equivalence and the agent-form implication; C07 proves the required realization and local-to-global steps independently.
PBE has multiple conventions. C07 defines only its explicit weak-PBE comparison and does not import a universal PBE hierarchy.
No source numerical example or equilibrium classification is reused. The chapter supplies its own fully specified off-path tree.
Printed pages 116–117 were read incidentally while locating the agent-form passage; no proper/quasi-perfect or generic-converse theorem is claimed proved or used.

proof_resolution: Full finite perfect-recall conditional one-shot lemma closes the source adaptation gap. C06 supplies proved finite perfection, not an asserted normal-form-to-extensive implication. Broader folk/reputation results remain explicit limits.
